title: PMP Eligibility Requirements in 2026 (Do You Qualify?)
dek: To sit the PMP you need 35 hours of project management education plus experience: 36 months with a four-year degree, or 60 months with a secondary diploma — counted from the last 10 years.

seo.metaDescription: Do you qualify for the PMP? The 2026 education and experience requirements explained simply, with all pathways and how the experience is counted.

sources.label: PMI — What the new PMP exam, launched July 2026, means for you

body.richText: The most common reason people can't take the PMP isn't the exam — it's eligibility. PMI requires documented project experience plus formal education before you can even apply. Here's exactly what you need, in plain terms.
Every pathway requires the same 35 hours of project management education. What changes is how many months of experience you need, based on your level of formal education.

body.caption: PMP eligibility pathways (2026, source: PMI). All paths also require 35 contact hours of education.

body.richText: As of recent PMI rules, qualifying experience can come from the last 10 years (previously eight). That helps people returning to project work after a gap.

It doesn't require the title "project manager." PMI counts time spent leading and directing projects — planning, executing, and delivering work with defined objectives. Many people qualify through project responsibilities held under other job titles, as long as they can describe and document the work.

items: Leading tasks, timelines, and deliverables toward a defined goal
Coordinating people or resources across a project
Experience can overlap across the required months but must be real and documentable
PMI audits a share of applications, so keep honest records of your projects

body.richText: Do not inflate your experience to qualify sooner. PMI verifies a random selection of applications, and a failed audit can bar you. If you're short, the CAPM has no experience requirement — use it while you build the months.

richText: Everyone needs 35 contact hours of project management education before applying. Today those hours can come from any eligible course or provider — PMI doesn't require a specific one — and the training can be live (in person or virtual, with an instructor) or on demand. A structured course like the Google Project Management Certificate or a dedicated PMP prep course satisfies this. Note that holding an active CAPM can also cover this requirement — one reason the

link.text: CAPM makes a useful stepping stone

body.richText: A rule change is coming. PMI has said that from late Q4 2026, live instructor-led PMP training — virtual or in person — will have to be delivered through an approved provider pathway to count toward the application. Approved pathways include Authorized Training Partners (ATPs), China Registered Education Providers, and eligible academic programmes such as PMI GAC ones. Training you complete before the change stays eligible under today's rules, and on-demand courses are not affected by it. If you're booking live training, check the provider's status first.

items.question: Do I need a degree to take the PMP?
items.answerRichText: No. You can qualify with a secondary (high school) diploma plus 60 months of project experience, instead of 36 months with a four-year degree. A degree just reduces the experience required.
